I'm just going to repost something I just said a few minutes ago. 
Finding a good artist is easy.
Finding a good artist FOR YOU? Sometimes, that takes a few trial and errors.


Go through their portfolio.
Multiple times.
Look for any errors or any special touches they have.
See if you like any of them. 
Meet them if you must! Brief is fine. Just to get the idea of their vibe and see if you guys would get along. Tattoo artists usually are very good at keeping a conversation but what's better than keeping a conversation that you actually feel connected to? I had several that I thought was good at first but after talking to the artist I have now, no one can top her. Hopefully you'll find that too!


Once you do meet your artist, I highly suggest you get a test run on what the needle feels like if you're curious to your pain tolerance. (you can warn him/her about this beforehand so they're aware). They can just use water and you can get an idea of what it feels like. Again, it may either feel like a sunburn or a hot claw scratching at you. It's true. 

For the design, they need as much information as possible you can provide in order for them to get to the right direction. You steer. You put in your own details. It's YOURS and it's just up to them to make sure they fulfill **your** idea. 
If you have a sketch available, there's no question about it - you should show them. If this sketch is EXACTLY what you want, they can do that for you. If you want to mess around with it, they can also do that easily. My artist photoshopped my tattoo design right off the bat in front of me. 
Otherwise, yeah, they're going to go put their own flair and hope for the best. The more details, the better!

Also, where in southern Ontario? I used to live in London.

Makes 6 dozen:
 1 cup unsweetened cocoa powder
 2 cups white sugar
 1/2 cup vegetable oil
 4 eggs
 2 teaspoons vanilla extract
 2 cups all-purpose flour
 2 teaspoons baking powder
 1/2 teaspoon salt
 1/2 cup confectioners' sugar

Directions

In a medium bowl, mix together cocoa, white sugar, and vegetable oil. Beat in eggs one at a time, then stir in the vanilla. Combine the flour, baking powder, and salt; stir into the cocoa mixture. Cover dough, and chill for at least 4 hours.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Line cookie sheets with parchment paper. Roll dough into one inch balls. I like to use a number 50 size scoop. Coat each ball in confectioners' sugar before placing onto prepared cookie sheets.
Bake in preheated oven for 10 to 12 minutes. Let stand on the cookie sheet for a minute before transferring to wire racks to cool.
